sections.heading: Sherman Bytes 1.0 patch notes
sections.body: Sherman Bytes 1.0 is the same pixel tank on a new engine. 1.0.0 moved it onto Fizlet with the same waves, drops and cannon, and 1.0.1 (30 October 2026) fixes drawing on 2× and zoomed screens and lets you drag the scoreboard.

ctas.label: How the games run on Fizlet

spans.text: Same game and rules. The engine update is the only code change.

items.text: Fixed: the game draws in the right place on 2× and zoomed screens.

On a 1.5× or 2× screen, the tank, enemies, shells and the bases' beacon rings drew too big and away from the page: the tank started off screen and enemies fired at empty space. Now the art sits on your tank and around the bases (checked in Chromium at 2×).
The scoreboard drags.
Grab the card anywhere that isn't a key, with mouse or touch. It stays inside the window, even when the window shrinks.
Easier-to-read keys.
The scoreboard's key labels pass WCAG AA contrast in light and dark.
Under the hood.
Fizlet 0.19.0 (was 0.13.0). The game is 33,601 B gzip (1.0.0: 32,606 B); the budget moves to 34,000 B.

spans.text: Sherman Bytes moves from the DOM VIRUS core onto Fizlet 0.13.0. Same game, same numbers.

items.text: Same waves, drops and cannon.
The wave clock and the airdrops keep their numbers, and the cannon still levels up at 20 and 60 XP.
A new scoreboard.
Score, wave, armor and scrap, the cannon meter, the Cover, Pillbox and Mine keys and a comms toast for waves, in the Board UI kit.
Bases show their health
as a level inside the button (full green at full health) and a beacon ring.
A base is the whole button.
A button half off screen keeps walls fitted to its whole box, and a letter exactly at the tank's radius now blocks.
Same seed, same run.
A step never allocates (tested: 20,000 busy steps with waves, builds, mines and pillboxes, no minor GC), and a run replays from its seed (tested).
Size.
32,606 B gzip (0.5.2: 26,994 B). The Board UI kit's CSS is 3,060 B of it.
